# The confusion scan

The author found that `listen` then `expand the steps` printed "The steps
unfold." and unfolded nothing, and suspected many more of the same:
behaviour that is right in the expected order and a no-op, a contradiction
or a dead end on any deviation. `demo_worlds/fire/scan.ts` looks for them by
machine. From the initial world and from every state along the acceptance
script it enumerates every command the parser accepts — the typeahead's
option list is the ground truth of what a player can tap — applies each one,
and compares the world's own fields, the whole story tree as a
tag-and-class signature (so a fold that folds nothing shows up as no change
at all) and the text the new frame printed. Scanning every state of the
script is therefore also scanning **every one-command deviation** from it.

**DEAD END is a reachability proof, not a look-ahead.** From the state each
command leaves behind, a keyed best-first search over *advancing* commands
(`remember`, `expand` and `collapse` pruned) must actually play its way to
the next scene boundary — the next `apply`, the next board closed, the next
beat. `reaches_end` chains those hops to l. 481.

Run it with `node scripts/confusion_scan.js` (`--every N` samples one state
in N); `tests/test_fire_scan.ts` runs it over a sample on every `npm test`.

## What was fixed

1. **`expand the steps` / `collapse the steps` before the notation exists.**
   They were offered from the first `listen`, one beat before Katya writes
   the notation, and set a class on a node that was not there yet: "The
   steps unfold." and nothing unfolded. Offered from the second `listen` on.
2. **The per-event folds are gone.** `expand <event>` / `collapse <event>`
   put one entry per transcribed event in the list — sixteen by the wise
   man — and buried the way on. `the story`, `the steps`, `the unmapped` and
   the chips remain.
3. **`collapse the unmapped` is offered only where it does something**:
   where some row is mapped and some is not. It used to fold nothing when
   every row was in the mapping and fold the whole column when none was.
4. **`speak as <voice>` says whose voice it is**: "You speak as the
   children." — before, it printed nothing at all until l. 350 taught the
   notation, and after that only the notation mark, which the board hides.
5. **`pick up the chalk`, `try the Pillaging …`, the `put down the chalk`
   that folds the attempt, and `draw a vertical line` on the wise man's
   board** printed nothing. Each says plainly what went up or came down
   ("The house in the woods goes up on the board.") — board chrome in the
   register of SPEC §8 [C5 D7], no Katya.
6. **`remember <classroom event>`** offered one entry per line said, and all
   but three printed the same "It felt like nothing in particular." (round
   5, player 2: "recall the first and second listening identically"). Only
   the three with a feeling of their own are offered now.
7. **"It felt like nothing yet. It has not been read."** → "It has not been
   read in any voice yet." (round 5, player 2 called the old phrase
   meaningless).
8. **The campfire trap ends with the way on**: "The friends do not command
   the fire, my dear. Let it follow." All three round-5 players stopped
   there.
9. **Several steps on one line.** Player 1 placed the campfire's steps 1–4
   and 8 and gave up after twenty attempts at 5, 6 and 7, because nothing
   says a line of a story may hold several steps. The stories now carry
   their own L4 defaults where the mapping shares a line: the campfire's s5
   and s6 ("It caught and it spread in one breath, my dear. One line of the
   story holds the spark and the spreading both."), the house's s5–s8 (all
   the scattering), the forest's s1 and s2 (all the dead brush). The wise
   man's literal pass already said it ("There are only two lines in which
   anything burns").
10. **The L1 nudge names what is missing.** It keeps its sentence and gains
    a plain list: "The Voice of Fire does not skip, my dear. The spreading
    of the ember is not on the board. Unplaced: the spreading of the ember,
    the spreading of the flame, the consumption of all."

**The author's unwinnable-state hypothesis** — "initial spread of ember if
the player chose sing before let it follow" — does not hold, and the scan
now proves it standing: at the campfire's ¶8 ("The fire starts…") the only
commands offered are `let it follow` and the trap; `sing` belongs to ¶9 and
a ¶'s command is offered only at that ¶. No consequence-only ¶ in any story
can be skipped or attached elsewhere, in the campfire, the house's four, or
anywhere else, so the transcription can never make a mapping unsolvable.
The scan found no state at all from which the next scene is out of reach.

---

## Remaining, by design

Nothing is reported any more. These are the things the scan deliberately
does not count as findings, and why:

- **A trap, a refused `map`, a `speak as` with no line here.** They print a
  nudge and change nothing on purpose (SPEC §13: "Available, printing a
  nudge, advancing nothing"; l. 540 wants the wrong attempt to produce a
  message). A command that prints is not a no-op.
- **`remember <anything>`.** A reprint changes nothing but the frame it
  writes; printing is the whole of it.
- **A chip expanded with no board open.** Only display commands and
  `remember` are offered there (SPEC §8's chip mode), which looks like a
  dead end for one step. It is not: `collapse the <story>` gives the scene
  back, and the scanner proves it rather than assuming it.
- **After l. 481.** The lesson is over: `say Ok, I guess`, the coda, and
  then only `remember`, the folds and the one optional attempt at the
  Pillaging. There is no next scene to reach, and that is the ending.
- **The Pillaging's steps 2 and 3 can never be placed** (SPEC §12: the
  .md's own gap — the children enter nothing and take nothing). Every
  attempt is refused with its nudge, `apply the Pillaging` always fails L1,
  and Katya says so once. Nothing about it gates anything.
- **`say that you see it` is Locked for ever** (SPEC §6). It is optional, so
  it never blocks the beat.
- **A mapping state offers one `map <step> to <event>` per pair** — up to
  250 options at the wise man's second pass. That is the puzzle, not noise:
  the commands that advance the scene are the first the typeahead lists, and
  the player types `map` and then a step, so the list they see is short.
- **SPEC §6's `expand <event>` / `collapse <event>` are not offered at
  all.** One entry per transcribed event (sixteen by the wise man) flooded
  the list; `the story`, `the steps`, `the unmapped` and the chips remain.
- **SPEC §10's "any other classroom event: It felt like nothing in
  particular."** is cut, as SPEC §12's cut order allows: only the picking up
  of the chalk, the drawing of the vertical line and the saying of Ok, I
  guess are rememberable now.

What the scan does **not** cover, and would want a bigger budget for:
deviations of two commands or more from the script (each state is scanned
for one-command deviations only, though the states reached by the script
already cover a great many); at one state, only the first few commands of
each verb get their own reachability proof, and a proof already made for a
state's key is reused; and a search that runs out of its four-hundred-move
budget reports a suspicion, not a proof of the contrary.
